skills.name: Energy: forms and sources, renewable and non-renewable

note.text:
Energy is the ability to do work. Unit: the joule (J); 1 kJ = 1000 J.
Forms: kinetic (movement), potential (gravitational: height; elastic: stretched spring), chemical (food, fuel, batteries), thermal (heat), electrical, light, sound, nuclear.
Sources:
• Renewable (will not run out): solar, wind, hydroelectric (Edéa, Song Loulou, Lagdo dams), biomass (wood, crop waste), geothermal, tides.
• Non-renewable (will run out): petroleum, natural gas, coal, nuclear fuel (uranium).
Fossil fuels release carbon dioxide and pollute; renewables are cleaner but some depend on weather.

sections.text:
Non-renewable sources took millions of years to form and will run out: petroleum (petrol, diesel, kerosene), natural gas, coal and nuclear fuel.
Burning fossil fuels gives carbon dioxide and other pollutants, which harm health and change the climate.
Renewables are cleaner, though some depend on the weather (no solar power at night).

mistake.right: Firewood is renewable only if trees are replanted as fast as they are cut
mistake.why: Cutting forests faster than they grow uses them up.

worked_example.problem: Classify these sources of energy used in Cameroon: firewood, the Lagdo dam, kerosene, solar panels in Maroua.
steps: Firewood: biomass, renewable if trees are replanted.
worked_example.answer: Renewable: firewood (if replanted), Lagdo dam, solar; non-renewable: kerosene

cards.idea: Energy has many forms; the unit is the joule.
example: A moving bus has kinetic energy; a battery stores chemical energy.

cards.idea: Renewable sources do not run out: sun, wind, flowing water.
example: Edéa and Song Loulou dams make hydroelectricity.

cards.idea: Fossil fuels are non-renewable and release carbon dioxide.
example: Petrol, diesel, kerosene, natural gas, coal

pick.q: What is one disadvantage of solar panels?
pick.r: They produce little at night or on cloudy days
w: They release a lot of carbon dioxide
e: They release no carbon dioxide when working.
The sun will shine for billions of years.
pick.y: Solar power depends on the weather and time of day.

pick.q: What is one disadvantage of burning fossil fuels?
pick.r: They release carbon dioxide and pollute the air
e: They give a lot of heat.
pick.y: Carbon dioxide contributes to climate change.

pick.q: What is one advantage of hydroelectricity for Cameroon?
pick.r: It uses rivers that are renewed by rain and releases little pollution
e: It needs a suitable river and valley.
pick.y: Rivers such as the Sanaga provide renewable energy.

pick.q: What form of energy does a stretched catapult rubber store?
e: Chemical energy is stored in food and fuels.
pick.y: Stretched or squeezed objects store elastic potential energy.

pick.q: What form of energy is stored in a plate of rice and beans?
e: Nuclear energy is in the nucleus of atoms such as uranium.
pick.y: Food stores chemical energy that the body releases.

pick.q: A mango hanging high on a tree has…
pick.y: Its height gives it gravitational potential energy.

pick.q: What is the SI unit of energy?
e: The watt is the unit of power.
The newton is the unit of force.
The pascal is the unit of pressure.

pick.q: Which source of energy is renewable?
e: Petrol comes from crude oil, which will run out.
Natural gas is a fossil fuel.
pick.y: Rain refills the river behind the dam.

pick.q: Which source of energy is non-renewable?
pick.y: Kerosene comes from petroleum, which forms over millions of years.

pick.q: Why is wood called renewable only if trees are replanted?
pick.r: Cutting trees faster than they grow uses up the forest
w: Trees grow back in one day
e: Wood is biomass, not a fossil fuel.
Burning has nothing to do with it.
pick.y: Biomass is renewable only when it is replaced.

pick.q: A girl climbs to the top of a slide, then slides down. Which energy change happens as she slides?
pick.r: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy (and some heat)
e: She is not storing energy chemically as she slides.
pick.y: She loses height and gains speed; friction makes some heat.

pick.q: A battery-powered torch is switched on. What is the main energy change in the battery?
e: That happens in a solar cell.
pick.y: Chemicals in the battery react to give electrical energy.

pick.q: In a hydroelectric power station, what is the order of energy changes?
pick.y: Water high behind the dam falls, turns turbines and generators.
